claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a high-temperature BCC state.
Rapid cooling from the high-temperature BCC state produces transient solute segregation.
Rapid cooling from the high-temperature BCC state produces short-range ordering.
Quench-induced solute segregation and short-range order act as nucleation sites for metastable phases during later aging.
Slower cooling permits more uniform solute redistribution.
Slower cooling preferentially produces equilibrium transformations.
A sufficiently high cooling rate inhibits complete diffusion of alloying elements.
Diffusion inhibition during rapid cooling promotes localized solute clustering.
Localized compositional inhomogeneities lower the nucleation barrier for metastable precipitation during aging.
Quench-induced heterogeneous nucleation sites cause a cascade of diffusive transformations and ordering events.
Cooling-rate-dependent solute distributions result in different phase assemblages after thermal processing.
Rapidly cooled samples will exhibit a greater diversity of metastable phases during subsequent aging than moderately cooled samples.
Rapidly cooled samples will exhibit a higher volume fraction of metastable phases during subsequent aging than moderately cooled samples.
More slowly cooled samples will primarily transform into the thermodynamically stable phase.
Moderate cooling followed by 10 hours of aging at 750 °C produces a predominantly uniform transformation with limited metastable-phase formation.
The proposed mechanism should cease to apply when slow cooling maintains a near-equilibrium solute distribution.
The proposed mechanism should not produce further transformation when aging conditions are insufficient to activate diffusion-driven transformations.
The cooling-rate thresholds and aging durations needed to generate substantial clustering and metastable nucleation are not yet known.
